title: Targeting instructor-cell voltage converts tadpole melanocytes to a melanoma-like state

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Targeting instructor-cell voltage converts tadpole melanocytes to a melanoma-like state

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In Xenopus tadpoles, briefly targeting the bioelectric state of a small population of instructor cells (with a chloride channel activator or a GlyCl mutant), in the absence of carcinogens, oncogenes or DNA damage, converts melanocytes throughout the animal, including distant ones, into an over-proliferative, invasive melanoma-like phenotype via disruption of serotonergic signalling.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: McMillen P 2024, Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates › Introduction › From normal melanocytes to a melanoma phenotype: a collective decision

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: This could be achieved in the absence of classical carcinogens, oncogenes, or DNA damage, by brief exposure to chemical (chloride ion channel activator drug) or molecular-genetic (GlyCl mutant) targeting of the bioelectric state of a specific cell population: instructor cells which normally keep the melanocytes in their healthy state via serotonergic signaling118.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: McMillen P, Levin M, “Collective intelligence: A unifying concept for integrating biology across scales and substrates”, Communications biology (2024), doi:10.1038/s42003-024-06037-4; section “Introduction › From normal melanocytes to a melanoma phenotype: a collective decision”. Scope: Xenopus laevis tadpoles

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-collective-05: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.67

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The perturbation, cell behaviors, and serotonergic mediation are measurable with established assays. Public reports support the phenotype but may not permit full reanalysis of every animal or exclusion of indirect systemic effects.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare melanocyte proliferation, arborization, migration, and invasion after instructor-cell depolarization versus controls, using lineage and serotonin-pathway interventions to test distance and mediation.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A melanoma-like phenotype is not equivalent to malignant melanoma.

Complete individual-level images and perturbation records may not be open.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Pigmentation extent, invasion and a serotonin rescue are measurable, and the instructor-cell papers report cohort incidences and images for chemical and GlyCl perturbations. Those files are not a public image archive, and Xenbase points at the experiments without holding the pixels. The phenotype can be checked against the published counts for this species, with the melanoma resemblance and the long-range mechanism only partly constrained.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After a brief chloride-channel or GlyCl perturbation restricted to lineage-labeled instructor cells, score melanocyte number, ectopic location, arborization and vascular or neural invasion in the absence of an oncogene, and test whether a serotonergic block prevents the conversion. Conversion of distant melanocytes without those classical triggers, blocked by serotonin interference, would support the account; conversion only inside the labeled instructor region, or no serotonin dependence, would weaken it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Hyperpigmentation can resemble a melanoma phenotype without a molecular diagnosis of melanoma.

Incidence counts and images are in the primary papers, not a deposited image set.

Genome-wide absence of DNA damage was not the published assay; the claim is the lack of an applied carcinogen or oncogene.
